content:
Apple celebrates its 50th anniversary this year, and many of its customers are older than the company itself. Apple has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, primarily through various accessibility settings.

From adjusting text size on Apple Watch to having your iPhone remind you when the washing machine has finished a cycle, the tips cover a wide range of uses…

Apple says the company is committed to making its technology accessible to everyone, including older users.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone — including older users. That's why our products and services are designed to be inclusive by nature — built-in accessibility features help you connect, create, and engage with everything you love, exactly the way that works best for you. Life keeps changing, and so does the way we interact with the world. From enlarging onscreen text to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to adapt flexibly to your needs.

The support page mainly introduces various accessibility features and is divided into ten major categories.

  • Vision: View your screen more comfortably
  • Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Customise how you navigate and control your device
  • Speech: Speak in your own way
  • Cognitive: Stay focused and in control
  • Personalisation: Create an experience that's uniquely yours
  • Organisation: Keep track of what matters
  • Health: Stay on top of your health with useful insights
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay in touch

Take the Vision category as an example — it includes features such as enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colours, setting colour filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing onscreen motion. Some features — such as Sound Recognition — were heavily promoted by Apple when first launched but remain little-known to this day.

Sound Recognition listens for specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when it detects them. The feature can recognise 15 different sounds, or can be trained to recognise your name, as well as unique electronic sounds in your environment, such as beeps from kitchen appliances, certain types of alarms, or doorbells. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay — your iPhone will listen for and detect sirens, car horns, and even a baby's cry. When a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — and if you're using CarPlay, the notification will appear on your car's display.

The page is an impressive comprehensive overview of the rich accessibility features currently available across Apple's devices. Each section provides guidance broken down by supported device, which may include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay, depending on the feature.
